problem_description: Proposals sat with the partners for over a fortnight because sign-off happened whenever two of them were free at the same time.
action_taken: Booked a fixed thirty-minute proposal review every Tuesday and gave one partner authority to sign anything under twenty thousand alone.
outcome: Time from qualification to proposal issued fell from eighteen days to four.

problem_description: Every proposal was written from scratch, so drafting alone took a week before anyone had read it.
action_taken: Built three costed templates covering the work the firm actually sells and reduced drafting to filling in scope and rates.
outcome: Drafting dropped to under a day; the review meeting became the only real wait.

problem_description: Proposals for public-sector clients stalled waiting on insurance and accreditation paperwork nobody kept to hand.
action_taken: Assembled a standing bid pack of certificates and policies and diarised its renewal dates.
outcome: The paperwork stopped being on the critical path.

problem_description: Work qualified in one week was still unpriced three weeks later because the consultant who scoped it was on client site.
action_taken: Made scoping notes a required field at qualification so anyone could price the work.
outcome: Pricing no longer waited on one person's availability, though quality varied until the notes template settled.

problem_description: A run of proposals waited on the client's own procurement process and the firm had no visibility of it.
action_taken: Asked at qualification who signs and by when, and recorded the answer on the engagement row.
outcome: Partly effective: the wait was unchanged but it stopped being counted against the firm's own turnaround.

problem_description: Proposals were revised repeatedly before issue because pricing assumptions were argued after drafting rather than before.
action_taken: Agreed a rate card and a discount ceiling once, in advance.
outcome: Revision rounds fell from three to one.

problem_description: Client reviews ran twice on most engagements because the first one surfaced questions the team could have answered up front.
action_taken: Sent a short findings summary two days before the review so the meeting confirmed rather than discovered.
outcome: Second reviews became the exception rather than the norm.

problem_description: Review sessions repeated because the client sent different attendees each time and each set asked the same questions.
action_taken: Agreed a fixed review panel at onboarding and required delegates to be briefed by their own side.
outcome: Repeat sessions stopped for the clients who agreed to it.

problem_description: The same review was logged twice on the tracker because both the consultant and the practice manager recorded it.
action_taken: Made the consultant the only person who advances a delivery milestone.
outcome: Duplicate entries stopped immediately.

problem_description: Reviews were rerun because feedback arrived by email after the meeting and nobody could tell what had been agreed.
action_taken: Wrote decisions into a single shared action log at the end of each review and had the client confirm it in the room.
outcome: Post-meeting drift largely stopped.

problem_description: A large engagement went through four review rounds because scope had never been written down precisely.
action_taken: Rewrote the scope as a numbered list of deliverables and reviewed against it.
outcome: Rounds fell to two; the client still asked for one extra.

problem_description: Reviews repeated on retainer clients because the same standing issues were raised every month.
action_taken: Split the standing items into a separate quarterly session.
outcome: Monthly reviews shortened and stopped recycling.

problem_description: Delivery reopened after sign-off because the client's finance team had never seen the assumptions the model was built on.
action_taken: Added a finance walkthrough before the analysis phase closes.
outcome: Reopened engagements fell to almost none the following quarter.

problem_description: Work went back into delivery after review because the brief changed mid-engagement and nobody re-priced it.
action_taken: Introduced a change note that pauses delivery until the revised scope and fee are agreed.
outcome: Scope changes stopped being absorbed silently.

problem_description: An engagement was redone because the data the client supplied turned out to be a stale extract.
action_taken: Made the client confirm the extract date and source in writing before analysis starts.
outcome: Rework from bad inputs stopped.

problem_description: Delivery reopened repeatedly on one account because the sponsor kept adding stakeholders who each wanted something different.
action_taken: Named a single decision-maker at onboarding and routed all requests through them.
outcome: Effective on that account; harder to enforce with public-sector clients.

problem_description: Findings were reworked after review because the consultant and the client had different definitions of the key metric.
action_taken: Agreed metric definitions in writing during onboarding.
outcome: Definitional rework disappeared.

problem_description: Work was redone because the draft went out before an internal quality read.
action_taken: Made a second-consultant read mandatory before anything reaches a client.
outcome: Client-visible errors fell sharply, at the cost of a day per engagement.

problem_description: New engagements started without a signed contract because onboarding began as soon as the client said yes verbally.
action_taken: Made a countersigned contract a precondition for opening the project code.
outcome: Unsigned work stopped.

problem_description: Invoices were raised late because the practice manager waited for the consultant to confirm the work was finished.
action_taken: Set a standing rule that a completed milestone is invoiced on the Friday of that week.
outcome: Billing lag fell from three weeks to under one.

problem_description: Inbound enquiries went unanswered for days because they landed in a shared inbox nobody owned.
action_taken: Rotated a named duty person for the inbox each week.
outcome: First response time fell to under a day.

problem_description: Time was spent qualifying enquiries the firm would never take.
action_taken: Wrote down three disqualifying criteria and applied them on first contact.
outcome: Wasted qualification effort roughly halved.

problem_description: Payments arrived late because invoices were emailed to the engagement contact rather than accounts payable.
action_taken: Captured the accounts-payable address at onboarding.
outcome: Debtor days improved by about a fortnight.

problem_description: The firm's shared drive had no folder convention, so files were saved wherever.
action_taken: Agreed a client/year/engagement folder structure and moved everything once.
outcome: Files became findable.

problem_description: Laptops were replaced ad hoc, so two consultants were running unsupported software.
action_taken: Put the fleet on a three-year replacement cycle.
outcome: Support issues stopped.

problem_description: Nobody was trained on the accounting package except the practice manager.
action_taken: Trained a second person and documented the month-end steps.
outcome: Cover exists for holidays.
